summary: Multi-input TOP that performs a selected composite/blend operation for each input pair. It can also pull additional TOPs by pattern, preview blend modes, pass through one selected input, transform the overlay relative to a fixed layer, and normalize output resolution/aspect/format through the Common page.

key_params.name: top
key_params.note: Additional TOPs to composite by path or pattern, such as ramp*.

key_params.name: previewgrid
key_params.note: Outputs a grid preview of available operation types with swapped-input variants.

key_params.name: selectinput
key_params.note: Pass through one input instead of performing composites.

key_params.name: inputindex
key_params.note: Input index passed through when Select Input is on.

key_params.name: operand
key_params.note: Composite operation such as Over, Add, Multiply, Screen, Inside, Outside, Maximum, or Subtract.

key_params.name: swaporder
key_params.note: Swap input order for operations where A over B differs from B over A.

key_params.name: size
key_params.note: Fixed layer used for final resolution/aspect and overlay transform reference.

key_params.name: prefit
key_params.note: Fit, fill, or preserve the overlay layer relative to the fixed layer.

key_params.name: extend
key_params.note: Overlay extend mode outside its bounds.

key_params.name: tstep
key_params.note: Translation step offset for repeated/pass workflows.

common_gotchas: Swap Operation Order matters for non-commutative operations such as Over and Hard Light; Add and similar symmetric operations are less sensitive.
Fixed Layer chooses which layer defines transform reference and final resolution/aspect, but it does not change the underlying Input1 plus Input2 composite order.
Use Native Resolution for pixel accurate composites when the overlay must not be stretched or squashed to the fixed layer.
The TOPs field supports Pattern Matching, so broad patterns can unexpectedly add more layers than the wired inputs alone.
Preview Grid is for inspecting operations; turn it off before using the node as the actual composite output.
